newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cabinet to discuss 1997 budget next week.
newsitem.headline: Romania cabinet to discuss 1997 budget next week.

text.p: Romania's government will discuss the draft 1997 state budget next week, after Sunday's parliamentary and presidential elections, a cabinet official said on Friday.
Government spokesman Ioan Rosca said Finance Minister Florin Georgescu had briefly outlined the draft 1997 budget before the cabinet but gave no further details.

"The draft will be discused next week taking into account proposals of executive officials," Rosca said, adding that after approval the bill would be then sent to the parliament which emerges after the polls.
President Ion Iliescu Romania's, in power since the 1989 overthrow of dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, leads in opinion polls for the country's third post-communist elections.
But his ruling Party of Social Democracy, is running second in parliamentary polls and a coalition government is almost certain to be formed.
A new cabinet might be appointed some time in December.
The January-August state budget deficit was 1.9 trillion lei. It is expected to hit 4.27 trillion by the end of 1996.

On Thursday, Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said the government emerging from Sunday's polls would have to cut spending and let its currency float freely if it wants fresh support from the International Monetary Fund.
Romania is represented by the Netherlands on the IMF's executive board.

The IMF withheld loan tranches for Romania earlier this year after expressing concern at restrictions on the local foreign exchange market and to show it was unhappy with slow reforms and lax budgetary discipline ahead of the election.

Last month the National Forecasting Board issued the key 1997 indicator estimates -- 5.5 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) and 20 percent year-on-year inflation -- expected to underpin the draft budget.
The 1996 official inflation forecast is about 30 percent but economists say the 12-month figure will be higher due to July price hikes and rising budgetary spendings.
The GDP growth is put at 4.8 percent this year. Year-on- year inflation quickened to 45.3 percent in September from 44.2 percent the previous month. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
